rows.location: course/modules/FC/FC2/cards.json FC2-c207 (new, L07) vs L07.html lines 119-122 (Def 2.1), 125-130 (Lemma 2.2), 132-141 (Theorem 2.3 and proof); L06.html lines 111, 138-141 (risk-neutral probability, Theorem 3.3)
rows.evidence: Card: 'Yes. Under A1 to A5 and A7, with r > 0 and h < σ²/r², V_n is e^{−rτ} times the expectation of the payoff max(S_τ − K, 0) under the weights q^(n), which are the tree's risk-neutral probabilities (Theorem 2.3, from Theorem 3.3 of Lesson 6).' Theorem 2.3 (L07 lines 133-137) states V_n = e^{−rτ} Σ_k binom(n,k) (q^(n))^k (1−q^(n))^{n−k} max(S (u^(n))^k (d^(n))^{n−k} − K, 0) under A1, A2, A3, A4, A5 and A7 with r > 0 and h < σ²/r²: the card's formula is that sum read as an expectation under the binomial weights, and its hypotheses match the theorem's statement. The proof (line 140) cites Theorem 3.3 of L06 with N = n and R^(n), giving discount (R^(n))^{−n} = e^{−rτ}. Definition 2.1 (line 121) gives q^(n) = (R^(n) − d^(n))/(u^(n) − d^(n)), the L06 risk-neutral probability q = (R_f − d)/(u − d) (L06 line 111) with R^(n) in place of R_f. Theorem 3.3 of L06 (line 140-141) is the multi-period pricing result with weights as in its Definition 3.2. Key-results row L07 line 366 says the same thing. The grade T is right: the statement is Theorem 2.3, proved on the page, and it rests on L06 Theorem 3.3 (T in L06's key results).
